Child 591d file impact lists `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/fsck_repair.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`, `tests/.../test_advisory_lock_ref_backend.py`, `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py`, 'focused new fsck/doctor repair ownership tests', `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`, `docs/release-notes.md` — it does NOT list `src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py` nor `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py`.

Child 591d ACs describe behavior ('Neither repair surface requires a `gh` binary'; gate-based fail-closed sequence) but never name `_repair_pause.py` as the gate owner nor `test_repair_pause_ownership.py` as the subprocess-rejecting test.
findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion 6 is measured in two specific named terms — the owning module `src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py` and the gh-rejecting test `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py` — but child 591d's declared acceptance criteria and file impact name neither artifact; the child delivers the behavioral outcome (no `gh` binary, durable gate ownership) but not in the parent's stated measurement terms.
scenarios: Completion verifier checks parent crit 6 by confirming `_repair_pause.py` owns the gate and `test_repair_pause_ownership.py` exists and rejects `gh`; child 591d's spec provides no declared file-impact hook to those exact paths, so the parent metric is measured against artifacts the child never names.

A reviewer submitting child 591d against its own file-impact list produces the ownership logic in a differently-named module or the gh-rejection assertion in `test_fsck_stale_channel_repair_heldout.py`, leaving the parent's named artifacts unsatisfied.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend child 591d to name `src/rebar/_commands/_repair_pause.py` as the module owning `refs/reconciler/gate` in its file impact, and add an AC/file-impact entry for `tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py` asserting rejection of any `gh` subprocess, matching the parent's crit-6 measurement terms.
